snippet.title: Dadi Ko Train Se Utar Diya 😢 Pota Kya Karega? ❤️
snippet.description:
Ek emotional Dadi Pota Story jo family love, trust aur apno ke liye ki jaane wali koshish ko dikhati hai. ❤️

Ek andheri raat mein Dadi apne pote ke saath last train pakadne ke liye railway station jaati hain. Pota apni Dadi ko train mein safely bitha deta hai aur ticket lene ke liye bahar chala jata hai.

Lekin Dadi ke paas ticket nahi hoti. Jab TT train mein ticket check karta hai, Dadi batati hain ki unka pota ticket lene gaya hai. Phir Dadi ko train se utarna padta hai. 😢

Dadi railway station ki bench par akeli baithkar apne pote ka intezar karti hain. Unhe poora bharosa hota hai ki “Mera pota mujhe lene zaroor aayega.” ❤️

Jab pota wapas aata hai, tab tak train ja chuki hoti hai. Apni Dadi tak pahunchne ke liye woh haar nahi maanta aur ek aakhri koshish karta hai. Phir jo emotional reunion hota hai, woh is heart touching Dadi Pota emotional story ka sabse emotional moment hai. 🥺❤️

snippet.title: eBay Bans Chinese Ham Radios, HRO Hack Update, $1Million Gift To ARRL, & FCC Enforcement Roundup
snippet.description:
Like my shirt? Get yours here! --- https://go.notarubicon.com/myshirt
In This weeks Radio Dork news:
Out of an abundance of caution and on the advice security experts, HRO (Ham Radio Outlet) has announced that the company is moving all online credit card transactions out of their internal systems and will now be processing customer transactions directly from their payment provider, completely bypassing any internal HRO systems. 
The change will store all credit card data directly into the payment processor’s system instead of HRO’s internal systems, adding another layer of protection for online shoppers.
The change follows an August 8, 2026 announcement that  RO had received reports of unauthorized activity on customer credit cards after making online purchases on the Ham Radio Outlet website. 

The ARRL has announced that they have received a one-million-dollar gift from Dr. James M. Galm, call sign W8WTS.
The money will support ARRL STEM education work in its Education and Technology Program and the Spectrum Defense Fund that protects amateur radio frequencies, with a large share of the gift being unrestricted and going to the Diamond Club general fund and the Second Century Endowment, so that those organization can operate far into the future.
Galm, a fifty-year ARRL member was first licensed in 1975. He is a retired electrical engineer and entrepreneur who co-founded LayerZero Power Systems and holds nine patents. He is a contester who often operates from the Caribbean station PJ2T and runs a public DX cluster. 
This gift places him in the ARRL Maxim Society at the Millennium level, matching the first million-dollar pledge made a few years ago.

According to a publicly viewable discussion at the MyGMRS.com online forums, eBay is now blocking the sale of all amateur radio equipment made by manufacturers that are on the federal Secure Networks Act list, regardless of the whether or not the item is compliant or not.
The forum discussion quickly devolved into an argument over which radio brands are "crap", but based on the online posting it does seem that eBay may be enforcing the new government restrictions on the sale of certain hardware, too broadly.

And now for the FCC enforcement roundup. Here is what the FCC got up to in the month of August, 2026.
The FCC had 18 total enforcement actions, 17 of those enforcements were against businesses, including Hytera and ZTE for filing late paperwork, seven $25,000 dollar fines against tech firms for failing to reply to inquiries, a $45,000 fine for a cable-company, and as reported by the Notarubicon News Network last month, the FCC sent a mean letter to the operator of the North Georgia GMRS Network for interconnecting GMRS repeaters, in violation of FCC Part 95 regulations.
And now the part that you've all been waiting for. The total, combined number of arrests, fines and jail-time sentences for CB radio, GMRS, and ham radio operators for the month of August 2026 was ZERO.

snippet.title: Radioddity HF-010 review: portable multiband vertical Ultimate POTA/SOTA Companion?
snippet.description:
In this video, I take a deep dive into the Radioddity HF-010, a compact and portable multiband vertical antenna designed for ham radio enthusiasts on the go. Whether you are into POTA (Parks on the Air), SOTA (Summits on the Air), or just enjoy field operations, this antenna promises a lot in a small package.

- Radioddity HF-010 Portable Multiband Vertical Antenna: https://www.radioddity.com/products/radioddity-hf-010
- My signal recorded by Darren M0DCX during his livestream: https://www.youtube.com/live/oh7_genmAlU?si=EHZQugzV2NgMh25B&t=2480
- 1300MHz Antenna Analyzer used in the video: https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_c3RTpvvN

I’ll walk you through:

01:10 – Unboxing and Build Quality: A detailed look at the package contents, material quality, the carrying bag, and individual antenna components.
12:14 – Setup and Tuning: Practical demonstration of base assembly, adjusting the coils, telescopic whip length, and radials according to the manual and analyzer.
35:18 – Performance Test: Real-world QRP contacts on 80m, 40m, and 20m bands (including a successful contact with Derren M0DCX in the UK).
42:15 – Final Verdict: Final evaluation of the pros and cons, experiences with narrow bandwidth on 80m, and overall impressions of the antenna.

The HF-010 covers multiple bands and its telescopic design makes it incredibly easy to transport. Watch as I test its limits and share my honest thoughts on this budget-friendly portable solution.

Key Features mentioned:

- Frequency range and bands
- Telescopic whip and base coil
- Tripod mounting and radials
- Portability vs. Performance

snippet.title: Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson weighs in on Flock license plate reading cameras
snippet.description:
Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson is defending the continued use of Flock license plate reading cameras, while admitting law enforcement agencies need stronger safeguards to prevent misuse of the information they collect.

Wilson spoke about the controversial technology Wednesday during a law enforcement think tank hosted by the University Circle Police Department in Cleveland. The meeting brought together law enforcement leaders from across Northeast Ohio, including representatives from the FBI, Cuyahoga County Sheriff's Department, and East Cleveland Police Department.

Wilson said Flock cameras can be an important tool for public safety, pointing to their use in investigating crimes and locating missing people. However, he said officers who misuse information obtained through the technology should face consequences.

"If you misuse leads or you misuse OHLEG (Ohio Law Enforcement Gateway), it's a fourth-degree felony," Wilson said.

Tyler Madden reports. --

snippet.title: My Dream HF Mobile Station! ATAS-120A/FT-891!
snippet.description:
Ever since I got my Technician and General in May of 24', I've dreamed of a nice HF Mobile station I could activate parks with from the comfort of my truck. Our Louisiana summers are brutal and our winters can be miserable.  I also like to do multi park roves.  This setup will allow me to do all I've dreamed of.
I saved up the funds and purchased my second Yaesu FT-891 and the Yaesu ATAS-120A antenna along with the LIDO RAdio L-Max 2.0 mounting solution.  With some great advice from Rob, K4MHD, it all came together.  
With this type of install, the 40m tune seemed to be the one wild card.  I got lucky and she tuned like a charm on 40m, 20m, 17m, 15m, & 10m.  I haven't yet tried 6m but I'm sure it'll tune just fine.

snippet.title: Ham Radio vs The Soviet Army: The 1991 Coup That Ended The USSR
snippet.description:
Free Video Course - The Top 5 Beginner Ham Radio Frustrations (and How To Overcome Them): https://hamradiolaunchpad.com/free

In August 1991, a group of hardliners inside the Soviet
government arrested Mikhail Gorbachev, sent tanks into
Moscow, and shut down the national news. For three days,
the country had no idea what was actually happening.

Except on the ham radio bands.

This is the story of R3A — an amateur radio station set up
inside the Russian White House while it was surrounded by
soldiers, run by ordinary ham operators who relayed Boris
Yeltsin's decrees to the rest of the country when every
official broadcast facility was under the plotters'
control. They got jammed by the Soviet military. They
moved 5 kilohertz up the band and kept going.

I've been licensed since 2010 and I had never heard this
story until a few weeks ago. It was sitting in a magazine
I've had access to the whole time.

This is a new kind of video for this channel. If you want more of
these, subscribe — and if you know a story about somebody
with a radio who did something interesting or important with it, 
let me know in the comments.

—

00:00  A plane leaving in 3 hours
01:23  The man who was never supposed to go back
03:07  "Mortal danger over the U.S.S.R."
04:42  Tanks on the streets of Moscow
06:04  The call from Yeltsin's headquarters
07:19  R3A goes on the air
08:54  The military starts jamming
09:35  The mistake

snippet.title: 10 GHz Doppler Radar Module with Dielectric Resonator
snippet.description:
The HB100 is a widely available low-cost 10 GHz microwave Doppler radar module.

It outputs a signal whose frequency corresponds to the Doppler shift caused by a moving target. The output level is extremely low, so some amplification is necessary, especially when detecting targets at greater distances.

The emitted RF signal at around 10.16 GHz is highly unstable and susceptible to external influences, much like my mental state. The instability of the RF signal is shown using the real-time analysis mode of the Rigol RSA814 spectrum analyzer.

Removing the metal shield reveals the frequency-determining element: a dielectric resonator.

These are small ceramic cylinders that, through some form of black magic, provide very precisely defined points of resonance.

Pretty cool, right?
